title: 1.1 Meet the People
unit_outcome: Understand and produce simple sentences about people, family members, and actions.
goal: Identify a boy, girl, man, and woman, then use he or she in a short identity sentence.
grammar_function: A + singular person; He/She is a + singular person.
prerequisite: No prior English is required; this is the first course lesson.
speaking_outcome: Say short identity phrases and connect a person noun to he or she.

cards.pedagogy_note: The first person arrives; a introduces one person with boy.
The same boy appears in different clothes so he refers to the person, not the shirt.
The first two anchors combine into the lesson's first complete sentence.
A second child joins the same meet-the-people sequence.
The same girl changes clothes before the learner links her to she.
The girl follows the same noun-to-pronoun-to-sentence pattern as the boy.
The story now introduces the adult male counterpart to the boy.
The adult male immediately receives the same he-is-a identity frame learned with the boy.
The fourth person completes the cast after the man.
The adult female immediately receives the matching she-is-a identity frame.
The learner first separates child from adult within the male pair.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para el niño.
cards.pedagogy_note: The boy story immediately grows from the noun to the complete sentence in a new format.
The matching female age contrast follows naturally.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para la niña.
cards.pedagogy_note: The girl now receives the same noun-to-sentence treatment as the boy.
All four people now appear together as distinct visual categories.
The known he-is-a frame grows from boy to man.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para el hombre.
cards.pedagogy_note: The man is retrieved from a fresh image before the story moves to the woman.
The four-person contrast returns at the final story character.
The matching she-is-a frame grows from girl to woman.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para la mujer.
cards.pedagogy_note: Recognition ends on the adult counterpart, ready for audio-only retrieval.
Audio removes the visible target text while preserving the first age contrast.
The complete boy sentence follows the noun while the choice set expands.
The female age contrast immediately mirrors the previous card.
The complete girl sentence mirrors the boy sequence in a four-image format.
The learner now retrieves the complete male identity sentence by ear.
The man is now recognized from audio among complete written sentences.
The complete female identity sentence follows in the same structure.
Listening closes by retrieving the woman sentence in a different response format.
Production begins with the shortest familiar boy phrase.
The boy story grows immediately from noun phrase to full sentence.
The learner expands from a noun phrase to the complete girl sentence.
The same frame transfers from the child to the adult man.

cards.prompt: A man. He is a man.

options.label: A man. He is a man.

cards.audio_text: A man. He is a man.
cards.spanish_translation: Un hombre. Él es un hombre.
cards.pedagogy_note: Two familiar thoughts connect the adult noun to its pronoun in one spoken turn.

audio_assets.text: A man. He is a man.
A man. He is a man.

cards.pedagogy_note: The adult woman completes the four-person production set.

cards.prompt: A woman. She is a woman.

options.label: A woman. She is a woman.

cards.audio_text: A woman. She is a woman.
cards.spanish_translation: Una mujer. Ella es una mujer.
cards.pedagogy_note: The final spoken turn mirrors the man pattern and completes the story.

audio_assets.text: A woman. She is a woman.
A woman. She is a woman.

cards.pedagogy_note: The learner supplies the pronoun for the first person in the story.
The second boy card completes the same full sentence from its final noun.
The matching girl completion follows with the answer position changed.
Attention moves from the pronoun to the linking word is.
Two non-contiguous blanks now require the learner to build the complete man sentence in order.
The next completion focuses on the article that introduced every person.
The lesson resolves with the matching two-step woman sentence and the same ordered construction skill.
